text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- LVMH luxury goods group to buy majority stake in world number one perfume retail chain DFS (Duty-Free Shoppers), for an estimated 12.6 billion francs, to reinforce its market share in Asia.
-- The BNP offer on CIC bank may be favoured by the French privatisation committee over that of Societe Generale.
-- Government launches a six-year information campaign on euro targetting opinion, public services, firms and banks.
-- Merger of computer services firms Axime and Sligos create new six-billion-franc turnover unit.

-- Daewoo Electronics chairman Soon-Hoon Bae says Thomson Multimedia research and development activities would remain in France, if his offer to take over the electronics firm as part of a Lagardere offer on Thomson SA were accepted. He adds that the immediate cost of the takeover for Daewoo would be around 10 billion francs.

-- European Commission accounting experts question planned transfer of a 37.5-billion-franc France Telecom pension fund into French 1997 finances on which the government relies to meet the Maastricht criteria on public deficits.
-- Alcatel Alsthom sells a 2.2 percent stake in building material manufacturer Lafarge to Lafarge itself.
-- BNP chairman Michel Pebereau in an interview calls for reform of the French banking system to halt distortions of fair competition.

-- Daewoo group founder and chairman Kim Woo Choong says in an interview he plans to invest 7.8 billion francs in Thomson Multimedia to improve productivity, adds would create some 5,000 jobs in future Thomson Multimedia-Daewoo unit.
-- Textile sector workers demonstrate against industry delocalisations to foreign countries.
-- Thomson-CSF says taxes held first-half net profit to 396 million francs, up from 364 million in the first half of 1995.
